rejections.reason: The flat-case sentence restricts both worldline classes to affine (straight-line) curves. Valid accelerated C² timelike curves in Minkowski spacetime, such as x(s)=o+s e₀+s²e₁ locally, are excluded.

The massive-sector P is not tied to the cited action curve: U is only called “its future unit tangent,” without specifying its relation to T=dx/ds. Define U=cT/√(-g(T,T)) (equivalently dx/dτ) along an admissible massive trajectory.

Fatal: the cited Levi–Civita theorem explicitly assumes ACω, but the statement and Facts omit it while using that theorem to supply the connection. Steps 1.1–1.2 therefore rely on an unstated premise.

F11 defines D_s via the pullback connection for a smooth curve, but the item assumes only a C² curve (and C² variations). Step 1.2 applies F11 outside its stated domain, leaving the covariant-derivative notation and variation argument unjustified for the claimed class.

Fatal scope gap: the cited covariant-derivative definition applies along smooth curves, but x and H are only C². The proof uses D_s(T/ℓ), D_sJ, and D_εT without defining the C² extension or strengthening the regularity.

F5 restates the pairing rule without its smoothness hypotheses. The variable-mass clause assumes only C¹ U and applies the rule to U, so the cited interface does not license that step; the C¹ extension needs justification or stronger hypotheses.

[F5] only establishes derivative rules for scalar functions on subsets of ℝ. Step 1.1 applies it to show tensor components on an open subset of ℝ⁸ form a C¹ vector field; that restatement is unsupported, leaving the local Lipschitz argument unproved.
The physics-domain example gives no units or c=1 convention for θ, xᶦ, L, or ℓ. State a consistent convention so the line element and unit timelike tangents have operational dimensions.

Reject: paths are in affine Minkowski A, while F1 uses g on (M,g,N). No assumption identifies A with M or states g=η in χ, so the clock readings do not follow. [Carroll, proper-time definition](https://arxiv.org/pdf/gr-qc/9712019).

[F2] is restated for any massive leg with velocity, but its interface requires a C² future-timelike worldline on an open interval in the constant-mass sector. The item supplies no such worldline regularity, so the momentum formulas used in both steps are unsupported.

F3 gives the speed–momentum relation for a C² constant-mass worldline in an inertial chart. The collision data specify only a massive momentum leg, with no such worldline or identification, so step 2.1 does not establish the daughter’s speed.

No parameter space or parameterized Hamiltonian/vector field is declared, yet the theorem asserts smooth dependence on “parameters.” The cited ODE interface gives that conclusion only for a jointly smooth parameterized field; the proof supplies none.

The regular-level dependency requires F⁻¹(q) to be nonempty, but the definition allows C=∅ because independence is then vacuous, yet says the theorem gives C its structure. Require C≠∅ or handle the empty case separately.

F2 drops the supplied theorem’s C² future-timelike worldline and inertial-chart hypotheses. The collision datum specifies event-local legs, not such a worldline, so that dependency does not license the shell and positivity claims as restated.
F4 attributes a canonical action-unit bracket convention to def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system, but the supplied interface states no such convention; this is an unsupported dependency restatement.

Step 6.1 needs nonnegative outer integrals where f may vanish, but local fact F12 only states the positive-lower-bound case. The stated fact does not license that inference; restate its nonnegativity clause.

The theorem is for arbitrary symplectic P, but its bracket assumption and step 2 use {·,·}; cited F7 defines that bracket only on cotangent phase spaces. No general bracket is defined here, so first-classness is unsupported on P.
The scope says no particle action is included, but the definition explicitly introduces the worldline functional −mc∫s dλ as a “length action.” The stated physical scope contradicts the definition.

It defines admissible variations but never states that the physical worldline makes the action stationary (vanishing first variation for every such family). Thus “stationary-action model” is named, not mathematically formulated.

F5 identifies the covector with the square-root fibre derivative only on stationary first-order triples. This arbitrary C1 curve is not assumed stationary, so the claimed canonical-covector agreement is unlicensed.

The metric does not specify a time orientation, yet [F1]/[F2] require a future-directed normal and future shell. Positive lapse and h prove timelikeness, not that n is future, so the chosen root and E_n are not licensed. State that increasing X^0 is future.

The title claims generic failure, but the proof shows nonclosure only for V(z)=λz, λ>0, at specific regular points. It defines no notion of genericity or proves a genericity result, so the title overstates the item.

The definition allows any symplectic manifold P, but its cited bracket convention is supplied only for cotangent phase spaces T*Q. The dependency does not license that broader scope; restrict P or define the bracket for general (P,ω).
Title defect: H=N E_n-cβ^ip_i. With β=0 and N≠1, the energies still differ, so “differ by shift” omits the lapse factor.
The item is classified as mathematics but depends on `def-sr-affine-minkowski-model` and `thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition`; mathematical items may not depend on physics items.

Step 1.2 applies F2’s integral triangle inequality to the Riemann integral from the FTC. The supplied theorem covers only Lebesgue integrals of L¹ functions, so it does not license that step; no Riemann integral inequality is established.

In the TD branch, the statement and step 3.1 use m, but m is defined only in the Pirani branch. The TD formula therefore contains an undefined quantity; define m there (for example, m=-g(p,U)/c²) to make the deduction well-formed.

Step 2 invokes [F1], whose interface assumes an oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold. The statement allows an arbitrary Lorentzian manifold, so that cited implication is unavailable under its hypotheses.

The SI-unit claim lacks a premise that S₀ has action units. As stated, it adds arbitrary real-valued S₀ to an action integral, so the formula does not establish [S]=J·s. Require [S₀]=J·s or omit the unit claim.
L1 misstates the supplied positive-spin-orbit interface as conditional on H10, which it does not include. This inaccurate dependency restatement is a defect.

Reject: H is quantified as an arbitrary smooth Hamiltonian, but the relativistic claim and proof step 1.2 identify it with the shell-reduced H=-cp₀ from [L2]. No hypothesis makes that identification, so the covariant-shell conclusion does not follow for the stated H.

F8 omits its supplier’s continuity-on-I hypothesis: on [0,1], a function equal to 0 below 1 and 1 at 1 has zero derivative at every interior point but is not constant. The local dependency restatement is false.

Step 1.1 propagates the initial TD condition using [F1], but the cited invariant theorem assumes TD holds along the solution; its interface does not establish preservation from an initial TD state. Thus the zero-spin branch and subsequent deductions are unsupported.

Step 2.1 is dimensionally ill-typed: r−r_c and η are lengths, while w is a speed, so the Euclidean phase-space ε mixes units. The proof compares η to ε and energy (speed²) to ε² without specifying coordinate scales or nondimensionalization.

[A1] misstates [[post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model]]: it adopts the BMT spin law and refers translation to an action postulate. The Lorentz-force equation follows only conditionally from [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]] for stationary finite segments.

The cited IVP interface defines systems, IVPs, and interval solutions, but says nothing about maximal solutions or extensions. The claim that maximality is in its sense is unsupported by the supplied dependency interface.

The stated orientation choice is not available for all such geodesics: reversing the affine parameter flips E and L together, so L/E is invariant. Counter-rotating equatorial null geodesics have L/E<0 and cannot satisfy E>0, L≥0 in the fixed φ convention; the statement overclaims
Step 1.1 says [L1] applies on every [0,t], but its interface requires a<b. For t=0 the interval is degenerate; handle that case separately and apply [L1] only for t>0.

A1 overstates the cited free-fall postulate: it applies to ideal freely falling test bodies under specified test-field, size, and self-field conditions. The static observers here are constrained and explicitly not free-falling, so this dependency restatement is inaccurate.

Fatal source error: in the cited 2011 Poisson–Pound–Vega review, §§22.1–22.6 cover gravitational buffer-region expansions and gauge transformations. The electromagnetic point-charge and self-force material is §§18.1–18.6; the remark mislocates its central source.

Reject: [pthm] licenses E=γmc² for states on a C² future-timelike worldline parameterized in an inertial chart. The example supplies no worldline or definition v=dx/dt, so [L1]’s energy premise is unsupported.

Reject: no unit convention or dimensions are assigned to s, r, or b. The physical scale of the claimed Schwarzschild ray example is therefore unspecified; state these as lengths and give the unit convention.

L3 conflates thresholds: the theorem’s ε_* comes from the Christoffel lemma, while admissibility guarantees g00≤−1/2 only up to min{ε0,1,(128C)^−1}. No supplied interface relates these ranges, so L3’s time-oriented neighborhood and step 1.2 are unsupported.
